title: Vacant home tax and rental protection by-laws
subtitle: Rental renovation licensing, rental replacement policy, higher property standards fines and tenant compensation concerns raised by delegates
overview: Council held a special meeting on its Affordable Housing Policy Program and approved all three policy pieces it had requested from staff last November. Council directed staff to finalize a Vacant Home Tax by-law, a Rental Renovation by-law and a Rental Replacement by-law {{vote:m1}}, {{vote:m3}}, {{vote:m4}}.

The vacant home tax will be complaint-based and apply to vacant residential properties, with any revenue beyond costs going to the Affordable Housing Reserve. The rental renovation by-law will require landlords to hold a city licence before ending a tenancy for renovations that need vacant possession. Staff recommended a version without extra tenant compensation, and Council adopted it. The rental replacement by-law will come back for approval in July, along with related Official Plan and demolition control changes.

Council also asked staff to review property standards and yard maintenance fines and repeat-violation fees {{vote:m2}}. Implementation costs will come from the Affordable Housing Reserve, with ongoing annual costs added to the 2027 budget. Staff will report back annually, and the compensation question is expected to return for further consideration.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to finalize and implement the by-law, report back annually, and put any revenue beyond expenses into the Affordable Housing Reserve {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.item: Property standards and yard maintenance fines
decisions.detail: Staff will review fines for increases in line with other municipalities, and review administration fees for repeat violations, to improve compliance {{vote:m2}}.
Council directed staff to finalize a licensing framework for renovations requiring vacant possession, starting in 2026 with annualized costs of $374,000 added to the 2027 budget update {{vote:m3}}.
Staff will monitor the effects of provincial Bill 97 and report back on any operational, financial or policy impacts for the City.

Council directed staff to finalize the by-law and bring an Official Plan amendment and demolition control by-law amendment in July 2026, with annualized costs of $193,000 added to the 2027 budget update {{vote:m4}}.

debate: Tenant advocates, legal clinic representatives and tenants supported the licensing framework but urged adding tenant compensation, such as rent gap payments and moving costs, as in Hamilton, Toronto and Mississauga. Several delegates asked Council to pass the staff version now and revisit compensation later.

Delegates criticized the alternative compensation option as complex and conditional on a vacancy rate below 3 percent and rent at or below average market rent. They said the overall vacancy rate includes new high-end rentals and does not reflect the shortage of affordable units. Councillors asked staff to look into a vacancy measure that better reflects affordable housing.

A landlord delegate and a realtors' association representative questioned whether a municipal by-law is needed given provincial changes under Bill 97. They said the City lacks data on how many notices led to displacement, and warned that costs could push small landlords to sell or defer repairs. Staff said gaps remain, including independent verification that vacancy is needed.

A delegate asked Council to clarify how the vacant home tax treats legally operating short-term rentals. Staff said licensed short-term rentals in Guelph are basement apartments or additional dwelling units alongside an owner's principal residence and would be exempt.

Delegates asked for public reporting on the vacant home tax, such as a dashboard, and for the first year to be treated as a pilot. A concern was raised that the rental replacement affordability period should last the later of 10 years or until the tenant leaves. Staff said they will report annually.
